claim_text: Y and N supervision learn different recommendation semantics.
supporting_table: Phase2B binary/canonical ranking; Phase2C overall metrics
candidate_scope: Base/Y fixed binary; N fixed candidates
allowed_wording: Y and N supervision support different interfaces and objectives.

claim_text: Dedicated supervision remains strongest for its corresponding task while M1 provides a unified multi-task tradeoff.
allowed_wording: M1 is a useful multi-task tradeoff but not a replacement for the strongest dedicated models.

claim_text: LLM-vs-SASRec conclusions depend strongly on training exposure.
allowed_wording: N-K0 leads at closest exposure while high-exposure SASRec leads in a separate regime.
forbidden_wording: SASRec or LLM is universally better.

claim_text: Harder candidate settings reveal limitations that canonical random-k5 obscures.
protocol: canonical random-k5; PopMatch-k5; k20; k50; order perturbation
seed_scope: seed42 candidate variants plus order seed43
allowed_wording: Candidate size and popularity matching expose ranking limitations.

claim_text: M1 calibration nearly matches Y-K0 binary performance.
protocol: validation threshold selected on validation and applied to test
allowed_wording: M1 nearly matches Y-K0 after validation calibration.
forbidden_wording: M1 is the best binary model.

claim_text: N-K0 remains above M1 under PopMatch-k5 and multi-seed.
allowed_wording: N-K0 remains above M1 across three seeds.

claim_text: Popularity and BPR-MF alone cannot explain N-K0/M1 PopMatch-k5 performance.
allowed_wording: N-K0 and M1 exceed Popularity/BPR-MF on PopMatch-k5.

claim_text: SASRec high-exposure advantage is mainly middle/head driven.
allowed_wording: High-exposure SASRec advantage is not cold-tail driven in this slice.
